# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->


ARcenso is an open-source R package that provides reproducible access to Argentina's official census statistics. Historical census results are dispersed across publications, scanned documents, and spreadsheets whose structures and classifications vary across census rounds, making them difficult to access, compare, and reuse in reproducible workflows. This project will expand and strengthen ARcenso as technical infrastructure for working with these data and prepare the package for distribution through R-universe and submission to CRAN.

The project will focus on two complementary areas: strengthening the package infrastructure and scaling its data-processing workflow. We will address package quality improvements identified through `pkgcheck`, improve internal data storage and data types, review and adapt the existing package functionality, and strengthen testing and documentation. In parallel, we will develop a reproducible and version-controlled processing and validation pipeline for incorporating historical census tables, combining R-based processing, automated checks, and human review.

The project will expand ARcenso's census coverage by incorporating the 1991 national-level tables and progressively adding data from the 1960 census and subnational tables from the 1980 and 1991 censuses. It will also deliver updated tests, documentation and reproducible vignettes, intermediate package releases, and a final stable release distributed through R-universe and submitted to CRAN.

The project will run for nine months, from January to September 2027. We request **USD 5,500** to support **245 hours of team work**, covering labor for package infrastructure, development of the processing and validation pipeline, expansion of census coverage, testing, documentation, and distribution. The resulting infrastructure will provide R users, researchers, public institutions, teachers, students, and other users of census data with a more robust and reproducible resource for accessing and working with Argentina's historical census statistics.
